title: Greek Slow-Roasted Lamb
subtitle: Lamb shoulder slow-roasted with lemon, garlic, and oregano
excerpt: A whole bone-in lamb shoulder is spiked with garlic, rubbed with lemon, olive oil, and oregano, then sealed under foil and slow-roasted for four hours until the meat falls from the bone. This is the lamb of Greek Easter -- simple, fragrant, and deeply rewarding.
sourceNotes: This style of lamb -- kleftiko in its wrapped form -- is named after the klephts, Greek mountain bandits who cooked meat in pits to hide the smoke. The long slow cook with lemon and oregano is the defining flavour of Greek Easter.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The lamb can be slow-roasted the day before and reheated covered at 150°C for 30 minutes.
recipe.temperatureNote: Start at 220°C for 20 minutes to colour the meat, then reduce to 160°C for the slow roast.

content.text: The foil seal is everything in this recipe. A loose or poorly crimped seal lets steam escape and the lamb will dry out before it becomes tender. Use a double layer of foil and press the edges firmly to the sides of the tin. The lamb needs to steam in its own juices.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Make deep cuts all over the lamb with the tip of a sharp knife, spacing them about 4cm apart.
Push a sliver of garlic into each cut as deep as it will go.
Mix lemon juice, lemon zest, olive oil, dried oregano, salt, and pepper to make a paste. Rub this all over the lamb, working it into every cut.
Place the rosemary sprigs in a roasting tin. Sit the lamb on top. Pour the stock around the base. Roast at 220°C for 20 minutes to colour the outside.
Remove, cover tightly with a double layer of foil, crimping the edges firmly to seal. Reduce oven to 160°C. Return and roast for 3.5-4 hours until the meat falls from the bone when pressed.
Rest for 20 minutes with foil loosely on top. Pull into pieces with tongs and two forks.

items.symptom: Meat is still tough after 4 hours
items.cause: Foil not sealed tightly, letting steam escape
items.fix: Seal the foil very tightly and add another 100ml stock. Continue at 160°C for a further 45 minutes.

content.text: Greece. Easter Sunday is the centrepiece of Greek family life. Whole lambs on spits, or shoulders like this roasted in village ovens. Eaten with roast potatoes cooked in the same tin in the rich juices from the lamb.
